Add rules to a custom **Number**, **Single Line Text**, or **Date** field so that values that break them are refused wherever the field is edited. All rules are optional, and a value must pass every rule you set. An empty value is never refused by a rule. To require a value, make the field required instead.

1. Add or edit a custom field of type **Number**, **Single Line Text**, or **Date**.^[[Add or edit custom fields](#add-edit)]

2. Under **Validation**, set the rules for the field's type:

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Number

- **Minimum** — The lowest value allowed.
- **Maximum** — The highest value allowed. It must be greater than or equal to **Minimum**.
- **Allow Decimals** — On by default. Turn it off to accept whole numbers only. The **Decimal Places** number option only changes how the number is shown.
- **Allow Negative Values** — On by default. Turn it off to refuse values below zero. While it is off, **Minimum** and **Maximum** can't be negative.

#### Single Line Text

- **Minimum Characters** and **Maximum Characters** — The length allowed. Every character counts, spaces included. Spaces at the start and end of a value are removed before the value is checked. **Maximum Characters** must be at least 1.
- **Pattern** — The format the whole value must match, for example `ENG-\d{7}` for `ENG-` followed by seven digits. Type a pattern, or select one from **Common Formats**: **Letters only**, **Digits only**, **Letters and digits**, or **Code such as ABC-1234**. The **Means:** line under the pattern reads it back in plain words.^[Supported: literal characters, `.`, `[abc]`, `[a-z]`, `[^0-9]`, `\d`, `\w`, `\s`, `?`, `*`, `+`, `{n}`, `{n,m}`, `( )`, and `|`. A pattern can be up to 200 characters. It can't start or end with a space, because values are trimmed before they're checked. Lookarounds, backreferences, named groups, inline flags, and lazy or possessive quantifiers are not supported, and the message under **Pattern** says which part is not.]
- **Example** — A value that passes your rules, such as `ENG-1234567`. Users see it as the placeholder in the field and in the line under it.

#### Date

Date rules are available on **Date** fields only, not on **Date Time** fields.

- **Allowed Dates** — Select **Any**, **Past**, or **Future**. **Past** and **Future** both include today. Today is the UTC date.
- **Earliest** and **Latest** — The first and last dates allowed. Both dates are included. **Latest** must be on or after **Earliest**.

:::

3. (Optional) Enter an **Error Message** of up to 500 characters to show users when a value is refused.

    Leave it blank to use the default message, which states the rule, for example `Enter a whole number between 1 and 100.`, `Enter 11 characters or fewer. Use the format ENG-1234567.`, or `Enter today or an earlier date.`

4. Check your rules under **Preview**, which appears once you set a rule. Type a value in the field as a user would. The preview shows **Accepted**, or **Refused** with the message users would see.

5. Click **Save**.

    **Save** stays disabled while a rule can't be saved, for example when **Minimum** is greater than **Maximum**, the pattern is not supported, or the example breaks your rules.

Values saved before you add or change a rule are not changed. The rule applies the next time the field is edited. If you change the field's type, rules that the new type can't carry are removed.

To compare two fields that users fill in on the same workflow step, for example a completion date that must be on or after a start date, add a step rule to the User Action step.^[[Step rules](/guide/workflows/workflow-step-types.qmd#user-action-step-rules)]

#### Where field rules apply {#where-field-rules-apply}

Under the field, users see the rule in a line such as `Enter a number between 1 and 100.` When a value is refused, your error message replaces that line. On a **Date** field, days outside the rule can't be picked in the calendar.

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html" when-meta="includes.inventory"}
- **Editing a field on a record** — The field keeps the value you typed and shows the message. Nothing is saved until the value passes.
- **User Action steps** — When users save or submit the step, a **Some values break a field rule** pop-up lists each field with its message. Nothing is saved. **Back to the form** returns to the form with the values kept and the message under each field.
- **Set Field steps** — A fixed value is checked against the rule when you configure the step, and a value that breaks it is refused when you save the workflow. Values from a formula or from AI are checked when the step runs.^[[What happens when the step runs](/guide/workflows/set-field-formulas.qmd#what-happens-when-the-step-runs)]
- **Registration** — The same pop-up lists the field, the form moves to the step that holds it, and your values are kept. The record is not registered until the value passes.^[[Register records in the inventory](/guide/inventory/register-records-in-inventory.qmd)]
- **Bulk edit** — The pop-up lists the fields that were not saved, and the edit returns to the fields step with your values kept. Changes to other fields that were already saved stay saved.^[[Edit fields in bulk for multiple records](/guide/inventory/edit-inventory-fields.qmd#edit-fields-in-bulk-for-multiple-records)]
- **CSV import** — A row with a value that breaks a rule is refused, and its error names the field.^[[Import records into the inventory](/guide/inventory/import-records-into-inventory.qmd)]
- **Document intake** — A proposed value that breaks a rule is not written. The record is saved without it, and a pop-up lists the fields to review on the record.^[[Record intake](/guide/inventory/record-intake.qmd)]
::::

:::: {.content-visible when-format="html" when-meta="includes.artifacts"}
- **Editing a field on an artifact** — The field keeps the value you typed and shows the message. Nothing is saved until the value passes.
- **User Action steps** — When users save or submit the step, a **Some values break a field rule** pop-up lists each field with its message. Nothing is saved. **Back to the form** returns to the form with the values kept and the message under each field.
- **Set Field steps** — A fixed value is checked against the rule when you configure the step, and a value that breaks it is refused when you save the workflow. Values from a formula or from AI are checked when the step runs.^[[What happens when the step runs](/guide/workflows/set-field-formulas.qmd#what-happens-when-the-step-runs)]
- **Create Artifact steps** — If a value breaks a rule, the step fails and no artifact is created.
::::
